cards.front: What should you know about sedentary lifestyle?
cards.back: A way of living that involves little or no physical activity, characterised by prolonged periods of sitting or lying down during waking hours. A person with a sedentary lifestyle does not meet the recommended levels of physical activity for health.

cards.front: What should you know about obesity?
cards.back: A medical condition where a person has excess body fat to the extent that it may have a negative effect on their health. Obesity is commonly defined as having a BMI (Body Mass Index) of 30 or above.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — sedentary lifestyle and obesity?
cards.back: 1. For Sedentary Lifestyle and Obesity questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Sedentary Lifestyle and Obesity to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
Low energy expenditure, excess calorie storage (e.g. Joint problems, diabetes, heart disease)
Weak heart, high cholesterol, fatty arteries (e.g. Heart attack, heart failure)
Inactivity, weight gain, poor circulation (e.g. Stroke, kidney damage)
Insulin resistance, excess body fat (e.g. Nerve damage, blindness, amputation)
No weight-bearing stress on bones (e.g. Fractures, disability)
Lack of muscle use and stimulation (e.g. Weakness, poor posture, falls)
Significantly reduced (e.g. Heart must work harder to supply oxygen to greater mass)
Reduced (e.g. Excess fat limits joint range of motion)
Reduced (e.g. Greater mass requires more force to accelerate)
Reduced (e.g. Slower changes of direction due to increased inertia)
Increased (e.g. Greater stress on joints, bones and ligaments)
Students often forget to square the height in BMI calculations. Wrong: "BMI = 85 ÷ 1.70 = 50." Correct: "BMI = 85 ÷ (1.70)² = 85 ÷ 2.89 = 29.4."
